structures.name: Vermiform Appendix
structures.function: Immunological role (gut-associated lymphoid tissue); reservoir for beneficial gut bacteria
structures.location: Attached to posteromedial surface of cecum, 2cm below ileocecal valve. Position variable: retrocecal (most common 65%), pelvic, subcecal, preileal, postileal
structures.innervation: Sympathetic: T10 spinal level (referred pain to periumbilical region). Parasympathetic: vagus nerve
structures.clinicalNotes: Obstruction of appendiceal lumen leads to acute appendicitis. Pain begins periumbilically (T10 referral) then localizes to McBurney's point (right iliac fossa). Rovsing's sign, psoas sign, and obturator sign may be positive.

structures.name: Appendicular Artery
structures.function: Sole blood supply to the vermiform appendix
structures.location: Runs in the free edge of the mesoappendix from the ileocolic artery to the appendix tip
structures.bloodSupply: Branch of ileocolic artery (from superior mesenteric artery)
structures.clinicalNotes: Must be ligated and divided during appendectomy to prevent hemorrhage. End artery with no collateral circulation - thrombosis leads to appendiceal gangrene.

structures.name: Cecum
structures.function: Receives ileal contents via ileocecal valve; absorbs fluids and salts; commencement of the large intestine
structures.location: Blind-ending pouch in right iliac fossa, below the ileocecal junction, often lies on iliacus muscle
structures.bloodSupply: Anterior and posterior cecal arteries (branches of ileocolic artery)
structures.innervation: Sympathetic: T12-L1. Parasympathetic: vagus nerve (CN X)
structures.clinicalNotes: Cecal volvulus can cause obstruction. Covered by peritoneum on all sides (intraperitoneal) with variable mesentery. Important landmark for right hemicolectomy.

structures.name: Rectus Abdominis
structures.function: Flexes trunk, compresses abdominal contents, depresses ribs, stabilizes pelvis during walking
structures.location: Paired vertical muscle strips flanking midline linea alba, from pubic symphysis to costal cartilages 5-7 and xiphoid process
structures.bloodSupply: Superior epigastric (from internal thoracic), inferior epigastric (from external iliac), lower intercostal arteries
structures.innervation: Anterior rami of thoracoabdominal nerves T7-T12
structures.clinicalNotes: Rectus sheath hematoma from inferior epigastric artery injury. Used as free flap (TRAM/DIEP) for breast reconstruction. Diastasis recti: midline separation post-partum.

structures.name: Linea Alba
structures.function: Midline aponeurotic raphe uniting bilateral rectus sheaths; attachment for abdominal muscles; herniation site
structures.location: Midline vertical band from xiphoid process to pubic symphysis, formed by interdigitation of aponeuroses of external oblique, internal oblique, and transversus abdominis
structures.clinicalNotes: Preferred incision site for laparotomy and laparoscopy (avascular, midline access). Site of epigastric hernias. Umbilical port placement targets linea alba.

structures.name: Terminal Ileum
structures.function: Absorption of vitamin B12, bile salts, and fat-soluble vitamins; immunological function via Peyer's patches
structures.location: Last ~60cm of small intestine, ending at ileocecal valve in right iliac fossa
structures.bloodSupply: Ileal branches of superior mesenteric artery via ileal arteries and arcades
structures.clinicalNotes: Crohn's disease most commonly affects terminal ileum (ileitis). Meckel's diverticulum within 60cm. Resection causes vitamin B12 deficiency and bile salt malabsorption.

structures.name: Right Ureter
structures.function: Conducts urine from right kidney to urinary bladder via peristaltic contractions
structures.location: Descends retroperitoneally on psoas muscle, crosses pelvic brim at bifurcation of common iliac artery, enters pelvis to reach bladder
structures.bloodSupply: Renal artery (upper), gonadal artery, aorta (middle), superior/inferior vesical arteries (pelvic)
structures.innervation: Renal, aortic, superior and inferior hypogastric plexuses (T11-L2 sympathetic, S2-4 parasympathetic)
structures.clinicalNotes: At risk during appendectomy, right hemicolectomy, and hysterectomy. Ureteric colic: colicky flank pain radiating to groin. Three natural constrictions: ureteropelvic junction, pelvic brim, vesicoureteric junction.

structures.name: Mesoappendix
structures.function: Peritoneal fold suspending the appendix; transmits appendicular artery and nerve supply
structures.location: Triangular peritoneal fold extending from the appendix to the lower part of the ileal mesentery
structures.bloodSupply: Contains and transmits the appendicular artery
structures.innervation: Autonomic fibers traveling with appendicular vessels
structures.clinicalNotes: Divided and ligated during appendectomy before appendix removal. May contain fat that obscures the appendicular artery.

structures.name: Ileocolic Artery
structures.function: Supplies terminal ileum, cecum, appendix, and ascending colon
structures.location: Lowest branch of superior mesenteric artery, descends retroperitoneally toward right iliac fossa, divides into ileal, colic, anterior cecal, posterior cecal, and appendicular branches
structures.clinicalNotes: Key vessel ligated in right hemicolectomy. Preserved during appendectomy (only appendicular branch divided). Landmark during laparoscopic ileocolic surgery.

structures.name: Inferior Epigastric Artery
structures.function: Supplies rectus abdominis and anterior abdominal wall; anastomoses with superior epigastric artery
structures.location: Arises from external iliac artery just above inguinal ligament, ascends medially to enter rectus sheath posterior to rectus abdominis
structures.clinicalNotes: Lateral boundary of Hesselbach's triangle (direct hernia). At risk in laparoscopic trocar placement - lateral trocars placed lateral to this vessel. Injury causes rectus sheath hematoma. Used as pedicle in DIEP flap breast reconstruction.
